policy_title: Incentivise use of new construction technology
stated: Reform UK will incentivise innovation in construction to speed up building through modular construction, digital technology, and building sites that improve efficiency and cut waste.

source.quote: Incentivise Use of New Construction Technology We will incentivise innovation to speed up building: modular construction, digital technology and building sites that improve efficiency and cut waste.

bearing_set.reason: Faster, cheaper construction via modular and digital methods plausibly increases net housing supply and reduces build costs, directly affecting affordability and stock indicators.

Adoption of modular construction and digital technology in a major, chronically low-productivity sector (UK construction) could raise sectoral productivity and business dynamism, plausibly lifting broader real living standards — a concrete supply-side mechanism distinct from the O1 housing-supply channel.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: O1 is the designed-for outcome (housing supply); O13 captures the sectoral productivity spillover. O4 (worker displacement from automation) is plausible but too uncertain in direction and scale without specifics on what incentives are offered or at what magnitude — left out. O6 (reduced waste) is mentioned but too incidental and unquantified to clear the non-negligible bar on its own. O12 (cost of incentives) could bear if the incentives are substantive tax reliefs, but the policy gives no detail on mechanism or fiscal size.
